title: Flip M4-B independent golden user journeys

statusLegend.EXECUTED_CLI: command reproduced on the accepted M3 baseline in this task
statusLegend.PARTIAL: CLI portion executed; web or planned M4 portion is specification only
statusLegend.SPEC_ONLY: web/M4 capability not available on the baseline; no execution claimed

journeys.title: First-time sample-project walkthrough
journeys.initialState: Fresh browser session, no wallet, no account, no saved project. A built-in audited half-adder sample and a miswired candidate are offered as clearly labelled pinned fixtures.
journeys.userAction: Choose Try a sample; observe both source identities and the connection summary; declare baseline as oracle or accept behavioural-diff mode; run Compare behavior on the miswired candidate; inspect the replayed witness; apply the predefined Fix mapping action; rerun; download the evidence bundle.
journeys.expectedResponse: First run returns DIFFERENT with a replayed counterexample (input bits 01; reference outputs 01; candidate outputs 10). After the fix, rerun returns EQUIVALENT, solver outcome UNSAT. Both verdicts are shown beside a HISTORICAL / pinned-fixture badge. The downloaded bundle carries project, manifests, witness and reproduction request.

trustFreshness.classification: HISTORICAL (pinned sample); freshness axis shown separately from verdict
trustFreshness.rationale: No new chain observation is made. If live RPC is unavailable the sample remains a demo, never 'live chain verified now'. With UNDECLARED intent the EQUIVALENT result is pairwise behavioural equivalence only.

journeys.failureHandling: RPC unavailable: keep the sample usable and display 'pinned fixture — no current chain check'. Missing witness replay: show UNKNOWN and block export of a trusted DIFFERENT claim. Mapping invalid: return to Compose with a pin-level error. Never blank the screen or lose the project.
journeys.accessibility: Sample button has an explicit label; verdict and freshness are text, not colour alone; the witness table has row/column headers; focus moves to the result region after comparison; status changes are announced in a polite live region; download has a descriptive link name.
journeys.provenance: CLI-equivalent steps executed on M3 baseline; web journey is a specification only because no M4 web application exists in this branch.

journeys.title: Live X Layer circuit import
journeys.initialState: User enters a processor address and decimal circuit ID. The session has verified eth_chainId = 196 and has a reachable, explicitly configured RPC endpoint.
journeys.userAction: Submit the import; wait for the read-only snapshot; expand the REF dependency closure; inspect numbered pins, widths, state count and the integrity manifest.
journeys.expectedResponse: A decoded circuit snapshot with numbered pins (no invented semantic names), a bounded REF closure, a manifest binding chainId/processor/id/block/netlist hash/environment hashes, and integrity.freshness = CURRENT for a genuinely fresh observation. The observation is labelled SINGLE_RPC.

trustFreshness.classification: CURRENT only for a fresh RPC observation; otherwise HISTORICAL
trustFreshness.rationale: Chain labels are never trusted from a URL; eth_chainId is checked each session. Single-RPC observation is not malicious-RPC resistance or multi-operator consensus.

journeys.failureHandling: Wrong chain 8453 -> WRONG_CHAIN before any state read; unreachable endpoint -> RPC_UNAVAILABLE with retry controls; absent circuit -> MISSING_REFERENCE; malformed netlist or bad ABI -> INVALID_INPUT; oversized REF tree -> RESOURCE_LIMIT. No partial result is presented as a complete import.
journeys.accessibility: Form fields have persistent visible labels and programmatic associations; chain identity, block and freshness are announced as text; long imports expose progress and a cancellable control; errors are linked to the offending field and focused after failure.
journeys.provenance: Executed against a LOCAL RPC DOUBLE reusing the repository's committed offline transport and archived M0/M0.5 bytes. No live X Layer call was made in this task.

journeys.title: Offline / historical fixture selection
journeys.initialState: No RPC configured or deliberately offline; the archived XOR#1/NAND#2 captures at block 76206482 are available as a pinned project.
journeys.userAction: Select the offline sample source set; compose and compare; attempt to export or promote the result as current.
journeys.expectedResponse: Verification completes normally but the report integrity.freshness remains HISTORICAL, checkedBlock is null, and the context states local replay of single-RPC assertions. A caller-supplied CURRENT flag in the import does not change this.

trustFreshness.classification: HISTORICAL; never CURRENT from cached input
trustFreshness.rationale: Freshness is an independent axis. Historical evidence stays reviewable and reproducible but cannot be badged current.

journeys.failureHandling: If revalidation is attempted without RPC, return RPC_UNAVAILABLE / UNKNOWN and keep the historical result intact. Never silently upgrade HISTORICAL to CURRENT.
journeys.accessibility: The HISTORICAL badge is text with a definition, not an icon or colour; the blocked CURRENT action explains why it is disabled in text; focus remains on the result region.
journeys.provenance: Executed on the pinned M3 baseline; no chain access.

journeys.title: Two-circuit composition
journeys.initialState: Two imported stateless sources (XOR #1, NAND #2) are available with numbered pins and matching environment context.
journeys.userAction: Map source outputs to target inputs by explicit numeric pin index, add restricted NAND glue for the carry inverter, choose output order, preview and compile.
journeys.expectedResponse: A deterministic TAP-02 netlist with backward signal ordering and explicit REF edges; the preview reports byte count, gate/REF counts, dependency identities and the exact pin map; the compiled candidate is the audited 81-byte half-adder.

trustFreshness.classification: No independent freshness for composition; inherits source HISTORICAL/CURRENT
trustFreshness.rationale: Composition proves only that a well-formed netlist was produced from declared sources. It does not verify behaviour or chain state.

journeys.failureHandling: Invalid arity, out-of-range pin or undefined source -> INVALID_INPUT before compile; forward reference or cycle -> BAD_NETLIST; unresolved source blocks any 'verified' report or export; user is returned to the mapping table with the offending pin highlighted.
journeys.accessibility: The mapping table uses real table headers, per-cell labels and keyboard navigation; errors identify row and pin in text; the preview is an expanding region with a descriptive name; no graph-only information.
journeys.provenance: Executed on the pinned M3 baseline; web mapping interaction is specification only.

journeys.title: Deterministic half-adder build
journeys.initialState: The audited XOR #1 + NAND #2 recipe with explicit carry-inverter glue.
journeys.userAction: Run the composition 100 times on the same pinned inputs and compare the resulting netlist bytes and truth table.
journeys.expectedResponse: All 100 builds yield the identical 81-byte netlist with SHA-256 0x3dbb65a615e1f12be2325bdcad12b4a970a7ef721311452b5e09ac255ffc23ce and the complete 4-row truth table.

trustFreshness.rationale: Byte determinism is a property of the pinned compiler and inputs. It is not a proof of intent, correctness or current chain state.

journeys.failureHandling: Any differing byte or missing truth-table row fails the journey and is reported with the first divergent build index; no average or partial pass is reported.
journeys.accessibility: The reproducibility result is expressed as text (100/100 identical, digest shown) rather than a green indicator; the digest is selectable and copyable.
journeys.provenance: Executed: 100 CLI compose runs in this task; the same digest is recorded in M3 acceptance evidence.

journeys.title: Equivalent refactor
journeys.initialState: A reference candidate and a behaviour-preserving candidate (the pinned half-adder pair), with an explicit input/output mapping and a declared relation.
journeys.userAction: Declare the oracle mode (trusted reference, previous version, or undeclared behavioural diff), confirm the pin correspondence and run Compare behavior.
journeys.expectedResponse: EQUIVALENT with solver outcome UNSAT, source and mapping validation PASSED, freshness HISTORICAL. With UNDECLARED intent the result reads 'same behaviour; intended correctness unknown'.

trustFreshness.classification: EQUIVALENT within pinned stateless TAP-02 semantics; HISTORICAL
trustFreshness.rationale: UNSAT proves pairwise equivalence under the declared model and mapping. It does not prove either circuit matches a real-world intention or is secure.

journeys.failureHandling: Timeout, worker kill or replay failure -> UNKNOWN, never EQUIVALENT; incompatible maps or missing reference -> INVALID_INPUT/UNKNOWN with a mapping prompt; an untrusted oracle is visibly labelled rather than silently assumed.
journeys.accessibility: The intent selector has a legend explaining each mode; the EQUIVALENT conclusion and its scope are announced as text; solver outcome and freshness are separate labelled rows.
journeys.provenance: Executed on the pinned M3 baseline.

journeys.title: Differing wiring with counterexample
journeys.initialState: A candidate whose declared outputs are swapped relative to the reference, with the same input map and explicit output correspondence.
journeys.userAction: Run Compare behavior and open the counterexample panel; replay the input in the local evaluator; optionally export the witness.
journeys.expectedResponse: DIFFERENT (CLI exit 1) with a replayed witness: inputs bits 01; reference outputs 01; candidate outputs 10; replay REF_BEAT_REPRODUCED; minimization HEURISTIC, explicitly not claimed globally minimal.

trustFreshness.rationale: A detected difference does not mean the user's circuit is wrong. Without a trusted oracle the report states only that the two behaviours differ.

journeys.failureHandling: If independent replay does not reproduce the difference, return UNKNOWN with WITNESS_REPLAY_FAILED and block export; if the claim is serialized with a non-replaying witness, the trusted consumer rejects it with INVALID_INPUT / WITNESS_REPLAY_FAILED.
journeys.accessibility: Witness bits are presented in a labelled table with bit indices and both output columns named; differing bits are marked in text as well as visually; the panel is reachable by keyboard and announced on open.
journeys.provenance: Executed on the pinned M3 baseline; witness bytes come from actual CLI output.

journeys.title: Unknown result from timeout
journeys.initialState: A valid comparison request whose solver deadline is set to the minimum supported 1 ms.
journeys.userAction: Run Compare behavior and read the result, reason code, coverage and resource metrics.
journeys.expectedResponse: UNKNOWN (CLI exit 2), reasonCode SOLVER_TIMEOUT, solverOutcome INTERRUPTED, coverage INCONCLUSIVE, no witness, no EQUIVALENT badge; the worker is killed and reaped.

trustFreshness.rationale: A timeout or resource ceiling is never evidence of equivalence or difference.

journeys.failureHandling: The failure is the expected outcome: keep the project, offer a higher allowed deadline (at most 5 s) or smaller gate cap, and allow rerun. A subsequent completed job must still work, proving cleanup succeeded.
journeys.accessibility: The status text reads 'Inconclusive — solver timed out' with the reason exposed as text; a spinner is not the only indicator; the retry control is focusable and labelled with the new budget.

reproducibleInput.webScenario: B08 loading, timeout and error states

journeys.provenance: Executed on the pinned M3 baseline with a real native worker timeout.

journeys.title: Changed dependency manifest
journeys.initialState: A previously completed comparison pinned to a specific reference manifest hash, followed by a simulated beacon implementation upgrade in the local double.
journeys.userAction: Revalidate the pinned manifest against the current environment; then attempt to consume the old claim with its original pinned reference hash.
journeys.expectedResponse: Revalidation reports freshness STALE (CLI exit 7) for the changed environment; the historical report remains reviewable but cannot be badged current. A consumer pinning a different reference hash rejects the report with INVALID_INPUT before recomputation.

trustFreshness.classification: STALE for the old evidence; historical report retained
trustFreshness.rationale: Dependency or implementation change invalidates current status without erasing past evidence.

journeys.failureHandling: If the environment cannot be read, revalidation is UNKNOWN/RPC_UNAVAILABLE, not STALE and not CURRENT. The user is told exactly which hash changed and that a fresh import is required.
journeys.accessibility: STALE is text with an explanation, not a colour; the changed hash is shown in a labelled, copyable field; the historical report stays available with an explicit 'not current' label.
journeys.provenance: C30 executed against the local double with a simulated beacon upgrade; no live chain state was changed.

journeys.title: Failed RPC import
journeys.initialState: Import configured with an unreachable loopback endpoint, 200 ms timeout and zero retries.
journeys.userAction: Submit an import or inspection for a valid circuit identity.
journeys.expectedResponse: RPC_UNAVAILABLE (CLI exit 4) with a plain-language explanation, a retry action and a clear statement that no current verification was performed. No cached result is displayed as fresh.

trustFreshness.classification: UNKNOWN / infrastructure failure; no proof verdict
trustFreshness.rationale: Transport failure is not a verification result and must never be promoted to EQUIVALENT or CURRENT.

journeys.failureHandling: Preserve entered project state and RPC settings; offer corrected endpoint/retry; switch to offline historical fixture if available, clearly labelled. Repeated attempts must not create partial manifests.
journeys.accessibility: The error is announced assertively, associated with the import control, and offers a labelled retry; the page does not lose focus context or clear the form.
journeys.provenance: Executed on the pinned M3 baseline using an unreachable loopback endpoint.

journeys.title: Invalid pin mapping
journeys.initialState: A comparison request whose outputMap references candidate output index 2 while only outputs 0 and 1 exist.
journeys.userAction: Attempt compose or compare with the invalid mapping.
journeys.expectedResponse: INVALID_INPUT (CLI exit 3) before any SAT work, with a message naming the offending pin index and the valid range. No 'verified' badge and no partial report.

trustFreshness.classification: Invalid input; no verdict and no freshness claim
trustFreshness.rationale: Undefined correspondence cannot be silently repaired by the engine or inferred from names.

journeys.failureHandling: Return the user to the pin table with the invalid row identified; require an explicit correction; allow the corrected request to proceed normally.
journeys.accessibility: The error names the exact field and index in text; the offending table cell receives focus and has an aria-describedby explanation; correction guidance is not conveyed by colour alone.
journeys.provenance: Executed on the pinned M3 baseline.

journeys.title: Evidence export and re-import
journeys.initialState: A completed comparison result with manifests, project definition and (for DIFFERENT) a replayed witness.
journeys.userAction: Export a portable bundle, move it to a clean environment, verify checksums and feed the captured claim plus consumer-pinned hashes into the trusted consumption path.
journeys.expectedResponse: A valid captured claim is recomputed and accepted (CLI exit 0) with freshness still HISTORICAL. Forged verdicts, changed reference pins, CURRENT relabels and non-replaying witnesses are rejected with INVALID_INPUT or WITNESS_REPLAY_FAILED. Bundle verification never makes a single-RPC report current.

trustFreshness.classification: HISTORICAL after re-import; trust comes from recomputation, not from serialized flags
trustFreshness.rationale: Evidence is a reproducible claim, not a signed proof certificate or a fresh chain observation.

journeys.failureHandling: Checksum mismatch, missing file or unsafe archive path rejects the bundle; changed implementation rejects the claim as IMPLEMENTATION_CHANGED; no secret or credential material is included in the bundle.
journeys.accessibility: The export link names the file and format; the verification result and every rejection reason are text; a machine-readable summary has an accessible HTML counterpart; downloads do not trigger-only status changes.
journeys.provenance: Trusted-consumption portion executed; `export` and `verify-bundle` remain reserved and return NOT_IMPLEMENTED (exit 6) on the M3 baseline.

journeys.title: Read-only structural pre-flight
journeys.initialState: A valid composed candidate netlist, a verified current fee read via TAPEOUT_FEE(), and no wallet, key or signing capability in the process.
journeys.userAction: Run read-only structural pre-flight and inspect the status, the current fee as observed, and the exact scope statement.
journeys.expectedResponse: Exactly one of STRUCTURALLY ACCEPTED, REJECTED with a precise reason, or UNKNOWN. A known resource-burn-stage revert is classified structural only; the report explicitly states that no transaction was broadcast, no burn paid and nothing was published.

trustFreshness.classification: Independent pre-flight axis; never an alias for verification verdict or publication
trustFreshness.rationale: Structural acceptance is not simulation success, mint success or onchain publication.

journeys.failureHandling: RPC failure, missing storage override or unrecognised revert -> UNKNOWN, never STRUCTURALLY ACCEPTED; a structural rejection names the failed check; the user is never offered a wallet or broadcast action.
journeys.accessibility: Pre-flight status is a labelled text statement with an explicit definition; the fee is shown with its observation context; the no-publication caveat is a persistent text region, not a tooltip only.
journeys.provenance: Not executed. `flip preflight` is a reserved M4 command and returned NOT_IMPLEMENTED (exit 6) on the accepted M3 baseline in C18.
